payloads.rule: FRANCHISE-DEBUT FALLBACK. For any team t and game g such that t has played no prior CONTRACT-SCHEDULE game before g (t's franchise-debut game), define rest(t,g) := cap (10) - the debuting team is treated as fully rested. This extends the domain of rest(.,.) to a total function over the real universe without altering its value on any row where a prior contract game exists. x(t,g) = (rest(t,g) + rest(opp(g,t),g))/2 is then computed unchanged by the frozen formula, using the extended rest(.,.). The rule applies identically whichever side of the row-pair the debuting team appears on (its own offensive row, or as opp(g,t) in its first opponent's row) - both rows of a debut game receive the identical resulting x. Affected rows: exactly 3 debut games (1611661331 vs its 2025 opponent; 1611661327 vs its 2026 opponent; 1611661332 vs its 2026 opponent) x 2 rows/game = 6 rows total (matches the auditor's measured >=6, including the fold-4/5 TEST rows for the two 2026 debuts). No other row is affected: only a team with zero prior contract-schedule games triggers the fallback, and each of the three named teams triggers it on exactly one game (its own debut).
payloads.precedent_cited: Same 'assign cap value (fully rested), deterministic, no active-set rule' convention already frozen for A23's bundle_OM opener rule (stage2b/P35_FREEZE_TASK_CARDS/SPEC.json, arm_id A23_rest_differential_contrast, bundles_frozen.bundle_OM) - the in-fleet precedent for a team lacking prior-game history in a rest-type feature. No new machinery invented; an existing frozen convention is extended to A24's card.
payloads.preregistration_decidable_note: The rule is a deterministic function of contract-schedule membership facts alone (does 't' have a strictly-earlier contract game before g) - it consumes no fitted parameter, no fold assignment, no training-set statistic, and no SEALED_RESULTS content. It is decidable, and here decided, before P38 unsealing and before any result exists.

It does not touch coef(x) or any other term. Both arm and null are fit over the identical, now-complete row set; the null simply omits the x term per term_removal, exactly as for every other row.
